verses.zh: 我―耶和华所膏的塞鲁士；我搀扶他的右手，使列国降伏在他面前。我也要放松列王的腰带，使城门在他面前敞开，不得关闭。我对他如此说：
verses.en: “This is what the Lord says to his chosen one,[NOTE:1]to Cyrus, whose right hand I hold[NOTE:2] in order to subdue nations before himand disarm kings,[NOTE:3] to open doors before himso gates remain unclosed:
notes: Heb “anointed” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NCV “his appointed king.”
The “right hand” is a symbol of activity and strength; the Lord directs Cyrus’ activities and assures his success.
Heb “and the belts of kings I will loosen”; NRSV “strip kings of their robes”; NIV “strip kings of their armor.”
verses.commentary:
45:1 "anointed" This is a title in the OT used for several kinds of people.

- for King Saul, 1 Sam. 12:3; 24:6

- for the people of God, Hab. 3:13

- for the Patriarchs, Ps. 105:15

- for the priests, Lev. 4:3,5,16

- for "the Coming One," Dan. 9:25; Ps. 2:2

It is used as a Messianic title developed during the inter-biblical period. The term "Messiah"
comes from the Hebrew term "Anointed One." Cyrus being called by this term shows that election in the OT
was primarily for service, not salvation.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE

▣ "by the right hand" YHWH is actively guiding Cyrus II. See SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣ "to loose the loins of kings" This imagery ("loose," BDB 834, KB 986, Piel
IMPERFECT) refers to loosening the sash, which either

- implies a man's garments were free-flowing which made it difficult to move (JPSOA footnote, "I made them helpless")

- the sash may have held weapons and they, therefore, dropped to the ground (cf. Isa. 45:5; NET Bible, "disarm Kings")

verses.zh: 我必在你前面行，修平崎岖之地。我必打破铜门，砍断铁闩。
verses.en: ‘I will go before youand level mountains.[NOTE:1] Bronze doors I will shatterand iron bars[NOTE:2] I will hack through.
notes: The form הֲדוּרִים (hadurim) is difficult. It may need to be emended to an original הָרָרִים (hararim, “mountains”), the reduplicated form of הָר (har, “mountain”). 1QIsaa and the LXX support an unambiguous text of “mountains.”
That is, on the gates. Cf. CEV “break the iron bars on bronze gates.”
verses.commentary:
45:2

NASB
"rough places smooth"

NKJV
"crooked places straight"

NRSV, TEV
"level the mountains"

NJB
"open gateways"

JPSOA
"level the hills that loom up"

REB, Peshitta
"level the swelling hill"

The NRSV is literal ("make straight," BDB 448, KB 449, Qere, Piel
IMPERFECT). It is also found in the DSS and LXX. "Mountain" may be imagery of problems
or fears (JPSOA, cf. Isa. 40:4; 41:15; 42:15; 49:11).

▣ "shatter the doors of bronze, and cut through their iron bars" These are all imagery that
YHWH will cause Cyrus II to succeed in his conquest over the walled cities of Mesopotamia and Palestine.

It is interesting that the historian, Herodotus, 1:179, mentions that the city of Babylon had over 100 brass gates.

verses.zh: 我要将暗中的宝物和隐密的财宝赐给你，使你知道提名召你的，就是我―耶和华、以色列的　神。
verses.en: I will give you hidden treasures,[NOTE:1] riches stashed away in secret places,so you may recognize that I am the Lord,the one who calls you by name, the God of Israel.
notes: Heb “treasures of darkness” (KJV, NASB, NIV84, NRSV); NIV11 “hidden treasures”; TEV “treasures from dark, secret places.”
verses.commentary: 45:3 "treasures of darkness" This is the hidden wealth of the empires of Mesopotamia and the Near East.

verses.zh: 因我仆人雅各，我所拣选以色列的缘故，我就提名召你；你虽不认识我，我也加给你名号。
verses.en: For the sake of my servant Jacob,Israel, my chosen one,I call you by nameand give you a title of respect, even though you do not submit[NOTE:1] to me.
notes: Or “know” (NCV, NRSV, TEV, NLT); NIV “acknowledge.” The common verb יָדַע (yadaʿ) means “to know.” Among homophonous roots DCH includes יָדַע II meaning “be submissive, humbled; be quiet, at rest” (cf. Job 21:19; Prov 5:6; Jer 14:18; Hos 9:7).
verses.commentary:
45:4 "For the sake of Jacob My servant,

And Israel My chosen one" Here we have the first of two reasons why YHWH used Cyrus:

- the restoration of His chosen people to Palestine

- He wanted the people of Israel to be a light to the world, Isa. 45:6. Israel was not a light so
God used Cyrus II (cf. Ezek. 36:22-36).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

SPECIAL TOPIC: ELECTION

▣ "Though you have not known Me" YHWH used Cyrus even though he did not know
Him. There is a play on the word "know" in Isa. 45:4,5,6. In Hebrew the term "know" speaks of
intimate personal relationship (cf. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5), not only cognitive knowledge. There is no merit on
Cyrus' part that God should choose him, but God used him for divine purposes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW (using mostly Deuteronomy as a paradigm)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN, D.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华，在我以外并没有别神；除了我以外再没有　神。你虽不认识我，我必给你束腰。
verses.en: I am the Lord, I have no peer,[NOTE:1] there is no God but me.I arm you for battle,[NOTE:2] even though you do not recognize[NOTE:3] me.
notes: Heb “and there is none besides.” On the use of עוֹד (ʿod) here, see BDB 729 s.v. 1.c.
Heb “gird you” (so NASB) or “strengthen you” (so NIV).
Or “know” (NAB, NCV, NRSV, TEV, CEV, NLT); NIV “have not acknowledged.”
verses.commentary:
45:5 "I am the Lord, and there is no other" This is an affirmation
of monotheism (cf. Isa. 44:24; 45:6-7,14,18,21,22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

▣ "Besides Me there is no God" This is another way of referring to monotheism
(cf. Isa. 44:6,8; 43:11). See Special Topic above.

▣ "I will gird you" This means "arm you." The weapons were worn on the girdle
(cf. Isa. 45:1). This is the opposite of Isa. 45:1d.

verses.zh: 从日出之地到日落之处使人都知道除了我以外，没有别神。我是耶和华；在我以外并没有别神。
verses.en: I do this[NOTE:1] so people[NOTE:2] will recognize from east to westthat there is no God but me;I am the Lord, I have no peer.
notes: The words “I do this” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “they” (so KJV, ASV); TEV, CEV “everyone”; NLT “all the world.”
verses.commentary:
45:6 "That men may know from the rising to the setting of the sun

That there is no one besides Me" Here again is the astonishing
prophecy that YHWH chose Cyrus II for the same purpose that He chose Israel, which was to reveal Himself
to all the world so that all the world might come to know Him (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 45:22-23;
49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23).

verses.zh: 我造光，又造暗；我施平安，又降灾祸；造作这一切的是我―耶和华。
verses.en: I am[NOTE:1] the one who forms lightand creates darkness;[NOTE:2] the one who brings about peaceand creates calamity.[NOTE:3] I am the Lord, who accomplishes all these things.
notes: The words “I am” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons. In the Hebrew text the participle at the beginning of v. 7 stands in apposition to “the Lord” in v. 6.

On the surface v. 7a appears to describe God’s sovereign control over the cycle of day and night, but the following statement suggests that “light” and “darkness” symbolize “deliverance” and “judgment.”

This verse affirms that God is ultimately sovereign over his world, including mankind and nations. In accordance with his sovereign will, he can cause wars to cease and peace to predominate (as he was about to do for his exiled people through Cyrus), or he can bring disaster and judgment on nations (as he was about to do to Babylon through Cyrus).
verses.commentary:
45:7 This verse has caused much consternation among commentators because it seems
to make God the creator of evil. Basically, what is seen here is the denial of a dualism in the universe.
This may reflect the Persian influence of Zoroastrianism, but we are uncertain of Cyrus' relationship
to this developed dualism. This verse is basically saying that there is only one causality in the universe
(see full note at Isa. 14:24-27). God is in control of all things. He uses evil for His purposes! This is another
way of affirming monotheism.

Verse 7 is a series of Qal PARTICIPLES relating to God's
creating activities put in contrasting pairs.

- forming ‒ BDB 427, KB 428

- creating ‒ BDB 135, KB 153 (see John Walton, ANE Thought and the OT, p. 183)

- causing ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

- creating ‒ BDB 135, KB 153

- doing ‒ BDB 793, KB 889

Be careful of taking one verse out of a poetic context and using it as the basis of a
doctrinal statement. Genre and context are crucial in proper interpretation!

SPECIAL TOPIC: ONE CAUSALITY

verses.zh: 诸天哪，自上而滴，穹苍降下公义；地面开裂，产出救恩，使公义一同发生；这都是我―耶和华所造的。
verses.en: O sky, rain down from above!Let the clouds send down showers[NOTE:1] of deliverance!Let the earth absorb it[NOTE:2] so salvation may grow[NOTE:3] and deliverance may sprout up[NOTE:4] along with it.I, the Lord, create it.’”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “let the clouds drip with”; KJV “let the skies pour down.”
Heb “open up” (so NASB); NIV, NLT “open wide.”
The plural verb should be emended to a singular form. The vav (ו) ending is probably virtually dittographic (note the yod at the beginning of the following word).

The Hiphil verb form (תַצְמִיחַ, tatsmiakh) should probably be emended to a Qal (תִצְמַח, titsmakh). The יח sequence at the end of the form is probably due to dittography (note the following יַחַד, yakhad).
The masculine singular pronominal suffix probably refers back to יָשַׁע (yashaʿ, “salvation”).
verses.commentary:
45:8 The prophet is using the crisis of his own day to foreshadow the future kingdom of
God (see SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY [OT]). In
context, this verse is influenced by Isa. 45:6, which means that this is the idealistic future when all believing humans
will know and worship God, which was the purpose of the original creation (cf. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ Verse 8 is a series of IMPERATIVES (i.e. prayers) directed toward God's created order.

- drip down ‒ BDB 950, KB 1271, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

- pour ‒ BDB 633, KB 683, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- open ‒ BDB 834, KB 986, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- bear fruit ‒ BDB 826, KB 963, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- spring up ‒ BDB 855, KB 1033, Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

YHWH ends the paragraph/verse with His summary statement of His creating power
(BDB 135, KB 153, Qal PERFECT)! This emphasis on God as creator introduces
the rest of the chapter (esp. Isa. 45:18). As He created the earth, so too, Israel. Creation has a relational
purpose (i.e. Gen. 1:26-27; 3:8).

Notice the goal is righteousness and salvation!

verses.zh: 祸哉，那与造他的主争论的！他不过是地上瓦片中的一块瓦片。泥土岂可对抟弄它的说：你做甚么呢？所做的物岂可说：你没有手呢？
verses.en: One who argues with his Creator is in grave danger,[NOTE:1] one who is like a mere[NOTE:2] shard among the other shards on the ground!The clay should not say to the potter,[NOTE:3] “What in the world[NOTE:4] are you doing?Your work lacks skill!”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] the one who argues with the one who formed him.”
The words “one who is like a mere” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons and clarification.
Heb “Should the clay say to the one who forms it,…?” The rhetorical question anticipates a reply, “Of course not!”
The words “in the world” are supplied in the translation to approximate in English idiom the force of the sarcastic question.
Heb “your work, there are no hands for it,” i.e., “your work looks like something made by a person who has no hands.”
verses.commentary:
45:9 "Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker ‒" We have seen several
allusions to the court scene literary model in Isaiah. Now "woe" identifies another prophetic
literary model, "the funeral dirge." It was a "grave" warning to those (Jews or Gentiles) who question
YHWH. In context, this strophe would refer to the shock felt by Judeans at the inclusion of Gentiles!

This shows the presence of some Judeans who reacted negatively to God's
way of handling restoration to Palestine (cf. Isa. 10:15; 29:16; 45:11; also note Jonah). They were upset
that God would use an unbelieving ruler such as Cyrus II (cf. Isa. 45:13). This is very similar to the prophet
Habakkuk's incredulous thoughts about God using Neo-Babylon.

▣ "Will the clay say to the potter" This concept of humans as clay and YHWH as potter
is common in the Bible, probably because

- humans are made from the dust or clay and will return to dust (cf. Gen. 2:7; 3:19; Isa. 29:16; Jer. 18:1ff; Rom. 9:20-21)

- it highlights YHWH's freedom to do with His creation whatever He desires and purposes (cf. Romans 9-11)

There are MSS variants here.

- with the potsherds of clay (MT)

- with the potters of clay (NEB, JPSOA)

- with the potter of clay (RSV, NRSV)

The UBS Text Project, p. 123, gives a "C" rating to #1. This means the committee could not decide
which option was original.

▣

NASB, NKJV
"He has no hands"

NRSV, JPSOA
"Your work has no handles"

REV, REB
"you have no skill"

NJB
"your work has no hands"

Peshitta
"am I not the work of your hands"

NAB
"what you are making has no hands"

LXX
"nor do you have hands"

NET
"Your work lacks skill"

This can mean

- the idols have no hands

- the craftsmen have no skill

- the vessel has no handles

It is best just to recognize the ambiguity and look to the other lines of poetry in Isa. 45:9
and Isa. 45:10 for a general contextual meaning. That which is created (i.e. a pot or an idol) cannot question the creator!

verses.zh: 祸哉，那对父亲说：你生的是甚么呢？或对母亲（原文是妇人）说：你产的是甚么呢？
verses.en: Danger awaits one who says[NOTE:1] to his father,“What in the world[NOTE:2] are you fathering?”and to his mother,“What in the world are you bringing forth?”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Woe [to] one who says” (NASB and NIV both similar); NCV “How terrible it will be.”
See the note at v. 9. This phrase occurs a second time later in this verse.
Verses 9-10 may allude to the exiles’ criticism that the Lord does not appear to know what he is doing.

verses.zh: 耶和华―以色列的圣者，就是造就以色列的如此说：将来的事，你们可以问我；至于我的众子，并我手的工作，你们可以求我命定（原文是吩咐我）。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says,the Holy One of Israel,[NOTE:1] the one who formed him,concerning things to come:[NOTE:2] “How dare you question me[NOTE:3] about my children!How dare you tell me what to do with[NOTE:4] the work of my own hands!
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

The Hebrew text reads “the one who formed him, the coming things.” Among various suggestions, some have proposed an emendation of יֹצְרוֹ (yotsero, “the one who formed him”) to יֹצֵר (yotser, “the one who forms”; the suffixed form in the Hebrew text may be influenced by vv. 9-10, where the same form appears twice) and takes “coming things” as the object of the participle (either objective genitive or accusative): “the one who brings the future into being.”
Heb “Ask me.” The rhetorical command sarcastically expresses the Lord’s disgust with those who question his ways.
Heb “Do you command me about…?” The rhetorical question sarcastically expresses the Lord’s disgust with those who question his ways.
verses.commentary:
45:11 This verse starts out with several titles for God.

- YHWH (see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.)

- the Holy One of Israel (see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE)

- Israel's Maker (BDB 427, KB 428, Qal PARTICIPLE)

It then continues the emphasis on YHWH as the predictor of future events (i.e. Cyrus' conquest).

The UBS Text Project (p. 125) suggests, "questions me about the things to come, (but) as
to my sons and the work of my hands, let me take care of them!" (JPSOA, "will you question Me").

▣ "My hands" SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

verses.zh: 我造地，又造人在地上。我亲手铺张诸天；天上万象也是我所命定的。
verses.en: I made the earth;I created the people who live[NOTE:1] on it.It was me—my hands[NOTE:2] stretched out the sky.[NOTE:3] I give orders to all the heavenly lights.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “who live” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “I, even my hands”; NASB “I stretched out…with My hands”; NRSV “it was my hands that stretched out.” The same construction occurs at the beginning of v. 13.
Or “the heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heavens” or “sky” depending on the context.
Heb “and to all their host I commanded.” See the notes at 40:26.
verses.commentary:
45:12 Line 1 reflects Genesis 1.

▣ "stretched out the heavens" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

▣ "with My hands" SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE TO DESCRIBE GOD

▣ "And I ordained all their host" Here again YHWH is magnifying His unique place as
Creator of heaven and earth. The Babylonians worshiped the stars and planets. This is a strong
statement that YHWH commanded (BDB 845, KB 1010, Piel PERFECT) all their
hosts (cf. Isa. 40:26; 48:13; Ps. 33:6). This emphasis on YHWH as the creator and controller of the heavenly bodies
(i.e. sun, moon, stars, planets, comets) functions like Genesis 1 in showing the folly of astral worship.

In Isa. 24:21-22 the word "host" is used for the angelic powers behind the nations
(cf. the LXX of Deut. 32:8 and Daniel 10). Whether it is angelic or planetary, YHWH is in control of all
the lesser spiritual beings of the universe called elohim. There is no other Supreme Being but YHWH,
but there are other spiritual forces.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANGELS AND THE DEMONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

verses.zh: 我凭公义兴起塞鲁士（原文是他），又要修直他一切道路。他必建造我的城，释放我被掳的民；不是为工价，也不是为赏赐。这是万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: It is me—I stir him up and commission him;[NOTE:1] I will make all his ways level.He will rebuild my city;he will send my exiled people home,but not for a price or a bribe,”says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “I stir him up in righteousness”; NASB “I have aroused him.” See the note at 41:2. Cyrus (cf. 44:28) is in view here.
verses.commentary:
45:13 "I have aroused him in righteousness" The NIV translates the "him" as Cyrus. YHWH
stirred up Cyrus to do His will. This refers to

- the rapid and complete conquests by Cyrus II

- the decree of Cyrus II, which allowed all the exiled people groups to go home and rebuild their
national temples. This decree was given in 538 B.C., one year after the fall of Neo-Babylon.

▣ "My city" See SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO CITIES IN ISAIAH

▣ "Without any payment or reward" YHWH will give Cyrus II victory and he in turn will
let Israel return to Judah without a bribe or payment (TEV).

The Jewish Study Bible (p. 876) says that Isa. 45:14 refers to YHWH's reward to Cyrus.

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：埃及劳碌得来的和古实的货物必归你；身量高大的西巴人必投降你，也要属你。他们必带着锁链过来随从你，又向你下拜，祈求你说：　神真在你们中间，此外再没有别神；再没有别的　神。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says:“The profit[NOTE:1] of Egypt and the revenue[NOTE:2] of Ethiopia, along with the Sabeans, those tall men,will be brought to you[NOTE:3] and become yours.They will walk behind you, coming along in chains.[NOTE:4] They will bow down to youand pray to you:[NOTE:5] ‘Truly God is with[NOTE:6] you; he has no peer;[NOTE:7] there is no other God!’”
notes: Heb “labor,” which stands metonymically for the fruits of labor, either “monetary profit,” or “products.”
Or perhaps, “merchandise” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “the gain of Ethiopia”; CEV “the treasures of Ethiopia.”
Heb “they will pass over to you”; NASB, NIV “will come over to you”; CEV “will belong to you.”
Restored Israel is depicted here in typical ancient Near Eastern fashion as an imperial power that receives riches and slaves as tribute.
Israel’s vassals are portrayed as so intimidated and awed that they treat Israel as an intermediary to God or sub-deity.
Or perhaps, “among.” Cf. KJV, ASV “Surely God is in thee.”
Heb “there is no other” (so NIV, NRSV). The same phrase occurs at the end of v. 18, in v. 21, and at the end of v. 22.
verses.commentary:
45:14 It is uncertain if Isa. 45:14-17 comprises a literary unit. It is obvious that Isa. 45:15-17 is
referring to Judah (cf. Isa. 43:3). It is possible that Isa. 45:14 may refer to Cyrus II and not to Judah.

However, these same nations are given as a ransom for God's people in Isa. 43:3. All the world was
meant to come to God in Isa. 45:20-22. Therefore, Judah could be the subject of Isa. 45:14. This is very
similar to the prophecies that all the nations will stream to a restored Zion (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 60:1ff; Ps. 72:8-11; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

The summary line of Isa. 45:14, "No other God," carries over to Isa. 45:16 (i.e. "they").
Both the idols and their worshipers shall be

- put to shame ‒ BDB 101, KB 116, Qal PERFECT

- humiliated ‒ BDB 487, KB 480, Niphal PERFECT

But Israel will not (cf. Isa. 45:17)!

▣

NASB, NKJV, Peshitta
"men of stature"

NRSV, NJB
"tall of stature"

TEV
"tall men"

REB, JPSOA footnote
"bringing tribute"

JPSOA
"long of limb"

LXX
"lofty men"

The MT has "men of stature." The JPSOA footnote mentions Ezra 4:20; 8:6;
Neh. 5:4 as corroborative historical evidence for the emendation.

- "men of" ‒ אנשׁו (BDB 60)

- "tribute" ‒ אשׁכר (NIDOTTE, vol. 1, p. 552)

Option #2 fits the context best but there are no textual examples.

verses.zh: 救主―以色列的　神啊，你实在是自隐的　神。
verses.en: Yes, you are a God who keeps hidden,O God of Israel, deliverer!
verses.commentary:
45:15 Notice the names for God

- God (El, BDB 42)

- God (Eloah, BDB 43) of Israel

- Savior (BDB 446, KB 448, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)

The Savior of Israel did hide Himself from His people for a period of time because
of their sin and rebellion (cf. Isa. 1:15; 8:17; 54:8; 57:17; Ps. 44:24; 88:14, also note Job 13:24). But
that period of judgment has passed (cf. Isa. 40:2) and now the return and restoration has begun
through Cyrus II.

The AB, vol. 20, p. 82, suggests this hiddenness is because Judah was a small
and insignificant nation at this period of time.

verses.zh: 凡制造偶像的都必抱愧蒙羞，都要一同归于惭愧。
verses.en: They will all be ashamed and embarrassed;those who fashion idols will all be humiliated.[NOTE:1]
notes: “together they will walk in humiliation, the makers of images.”
verses.commentary:
45:16 See note at Isa. 45:14. Verse 16 is theologically parallel to Isa. 44:11.

▣ "put to shame" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SHAME

verses.zh: 惟有以色列必蒙耶和华的拯救，得永远的救恩。你们必不蒙羞，也不抱愧，直到永世无尽。
verses.en: Israel will be delivered once and for all by the Lord;[NOTE:1] you will never again be ashamed or humiliated.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Israel will be delivered by the Lord [with] a permanent deliverance.”
Heb “you will not be ashamed and you will not be humiliated for ages of future time.”
verses.commentary:
45:17 This is a wonderful promise but readers need to remember it is conditional on
Judah's covenant obedience. Just to read this and forget that Israel was again conquered and
destroyed by both Greece and Rome shows the limits of proof-texting.

The problem was not YHWH's love, power, and promises, but Israel's inability to keep
His commandments. See SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

The Hebrew terms "everlasting" (BDB 761) and "eternity" (BDB 761) are from
a Hebrew root that has a wide range of meaning (i.e. semantic field).

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

verses.zh: 创造诸天的耶和华，制造成全大地的　神，他创造坚定大地，并非使地荒凉，是要给人居住。他如此说：我是耶和华，再没有别神。
verses.en: For this is what the Lord says,the one who created the sky—he is the true God,[NOTE:1] the one who formed the earth and made it;he established it,he did not create it without order,[NOTE:2] he formed it to be inhabited:“I am the Lord, I have no peer.
notes: Heb “he [is] the God.” The article here indicates uniqueness.
Or “unformed.” Gen 1:2 describes the world as “unformed” (תֹהוּ, tohu) prior to God’s creative work, but God then formed the world and made it fit for habitation.
verses.commentary:
45:18 "He established it and did not create it a waste place" This is an allusion to
Gen. 1:2. It could be translated "without form" (BDB 1062). YHWH always had a purpose for this planet. That
purpose is that it would be inhabited (i.e. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7). There was a purposful, planned development in
God's creation. This does not prove some kind of destruction between Genesis 1:1 and 1:2 (i.e. the Gap Theory).
See full note at Gen. 1:1-2 online. I have been blessed by a new understanding of Genesis 1; see John H. Walton,
The Lost World of Genesis One: An Ancient Cosmology. This book sees Genesis 1 as Elohim preparing
this planet for human population. Dr. Walton views this text in light of other ANE cosmologies and concludes that it is
not addressing initial creation, but organization.

▣ "But formed it to be inhabited)" This is used by the rabbis to stress that
everyone should marry (cf. Gen. 1:28; 9:1,7).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CELIBACY AND MARRIAGE

verses.zh: 我没有在隐密黑暗之地说话；我没有对雅各的后裔说：你们寻求我是徒然的。我―耶和华所讲的是公义，所说的是正直。
verses.en: I have not spoken in secret,in some hidden place.[NOTE:1] I did not tell Jacob’s descendants,‘Seek me in vain!’[NOTE:2] I am the Lord,the one who speaks honestly,who makes reliable announcements.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in a place of a land of darkness” (ASV similar); NASB “in some dark land.”
“In vain” translates תֹהוּ (tohu), used here as an adverbial accusative: “for nothing.”

The translation above assumes that צֶדֶק (tsedeq) and מֵישָׁרִים (mesharim) are adverbial accusatives (see 33:15). If they are taken as direct objects, indicating the content of what is spoken, one might translate, “who proclaims deliverance, who announces justice.”
verses.commentary:
45:19 YHWH has asserted over and over in this section of Isaiah that He is the God who hears
and acts; Who knows the future and sets its course! This theological assertion is a primary evidence of
His existence! The other evidence is the existence of Israel and her return to the Promised Land.

verses.zh: 你们从列国逃脱的人，要一同聚集前来。那些抬着雕刻木偶、祷告不能救人之神的，毫无知识。
verses.en: Gather together and come!Approach together, you refugees from the nations.Those who carry wooden idols know nothing,those who pray to a god that cannot deliver.
verses.commentary:
45:20 "Gather yourselves and come;

Draw near together, you fugitives of the nations;

They have no knowledge"

Some say this refers to scattered, exiled Israelites returning home (i.e.,"you
fugitives of the nations," also note Isa. 45:25), while others believe it is another general invitation
to the Gentile nations, as in Isa. 45:6,22,23 (cf. Rom. 14:11; Phil. 2:10). Both are possible in this context.

There is a series of commands in Isa. 45:20-22 related to how humans are to approach
YHWH and respond to His offer of availability.

- gather yourselves ‒ BDB 867, KB 1062, Niphal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20

- come ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20

- draw near ‒ BDB 620, KB 670, Hiphil IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:20

- turn to Me ‒ BDB 815, KB 937, Qal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:22

- be saved ‒ BDB 446, KB 448, Niphal IMPERATIVE, Isa. 45:22

The NT uses Isa. 45:23 in two quotes that refer to all humans (i.e. Rom. 14:11 and esp. Phil. 2:10)!
What a wonderful invitation and fulfillment of Gen. 3:15 and 12:3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "Who carry about their wooden idol" This is a recurrent call on the nations to reject their idols
who cannot see, hear, or act, and come to the God of Israel who can act and who will save them.

verses.zh: 你们要述说陈明你们的理，让他们彼此商议。谁从古时指明？谁从上古述说？不是我―耶和华吗？除了我以外，再没有　神；我是公义的　神，又是救主；除了我以外，再没有别神。
verses.en: Tell me! Present the evidence![NOTE:1] Let them consult with one another.Who predicted this in the past?Who announced it beforehand?Was it not I, the Lord?I have no peer, there is no God but me,a God who vindicates and delivers;[NOTE:2] there is none but me.
notes: Heb “Declare! Bring near!”; NASB “Declare and set forth your case.” See 41:21.
Or “a righteous God and deliverer”; NASB, NIV, NRSV “a righteous God and a Savior.”
verses.commentary:
45:21 This is the imagery of a court scene. It predicts

- Cyrus II and his success

- the return of Israel as an evangelistic tool to bring the world to God

Here, God is called a "Savior" and in this context implies not of Jews only but of
the entire world (cf. Isa. 45:22; 49:6; 51:4; 52:10; Acts 13:47). The obvious implication of monotheism
is that the One God loves all humans created in His image (cf. Gen. 1:26-27).

verses.zh: 地极的人都当仰望我，就必得救；因为我是　神，再没有别神。
verses.en: Turn to me so you can be delivered,[NOTE:1] all you who live in the earth’s remote regions!For I am God, and I have no peer.
notes: The Niphal imperative with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose after the preceding imperative. The Niphal probably has a tolerative sense, “allow yourselves to be delivered, accept help.”
verses.commentary:
45:22 "Turn to Me" This is the Hebrew word that is used for worship (BDB 815, KB 937, Qal
IMPERATIVE PLURAL). As the people turn to God they leave their idolatry and sin (cf. Isa. 55:7).

Humans have a choice. They can turn to YHWH and be saved or turn to idols
(cf. Lev. 19:4,31; 20:6; Deut. 31:18,20) and have no hope!

This is a wonderful invitation for the nations to be included in the Family of God!

▣ "and be saved, all the ends of the earth" This is a reference to the universal salvation
offered to all humans who will repent and trust in YHWH because there is no other God (cf. Isa. 45:21). This
universal offer is so characteristic of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 25:6-9; 42:6-12; 49:5-6; 51:4-5; 60:1-3; 66:23).

This can be translated "save themselves" (Niphal IMPERATIVE),
which would be a play on Gen. 12:3 (see exegetical notes online).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 我指着自己起誓，我口所出的话是凭公义，并不反回：万膝必向我跪拜；万口必凭我起誓。
verses.en: I solemnly make this oath[NOTE:1]—what I say is true and reliable:[NOTE:2] ‘Surely every knee will bow to me,every tongue will solemnly affirm;[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “I swear by myself”; KJV, NASB “have sworn.”
Heb “a word goes out from my mouth [in] truth and will not return.”
Heb “swear” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV); NLT “confess allegiance.”
verses.commentary:
45:23 "I have sworn by Myself" There is no higher oath possible! This, of course, is imagery
for God's truthfulness

▣ "The word has gone forth from My mouth in righteousness

And will not turn back" This is the ancient belief in the power
of the spoken word (cf. Isa. 24:3; 25:8; 40:8; 55:10-11). God said it; He wants the world to be saved
(i.e. John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:2; 4:14)!

▣ "That to Me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear allegiance" There are several different
ways (i.e. physical positions) that ANE people worshiped.

- standing up ‒ 1 Sam. 1:26; 1 Kgs. 8:22; Jer. 18:20

- kneeling ‒ 1 Kgs. 8:54; 2 Chr. 6:13; Ps. 95:6; Isa. 45:23; Dan. 6:10-11

- prostrated ‒ Ps. 5:7; 95:6; 99:5,9; 138:2

A good example of multiple positions based on which part of the worship event is Nehemiah 9:2-5.

- they stood while Torah was read

- they knelt down to confess their sin

- they stood up again at the direction of the Levite leaders

This is used in
this context of YHWH. However, in Phil. 2:10 it is used of all conscious creation confessing Jesus Christ as
Lord. The context again shows that God wants the whole world to come to Him and later revelation will show
it is through His Messiah, Jesus Christ, that this universal offer is accomplished (cf. Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE GOSPEL).

The theological issue is very clear. If the NT is revelation, then the OT promises to national
Israel have been widened. Neither Jesus nor any NT writer ever reaffirms a national promise to Israel!

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE OT COVENANT PROMISES SO DIFFERENT FROM NT COVENANT PROMISES?

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO ISAIAH 44:24-45:25

- This is a very specific prophecy. Cyrus II, also known as Cyrus "the Great," is mentioned by
name in Isa. 44:28 and 45:1. YHWH has claimed several times that He knows and controls events
(cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 44:7,26). This prophecy is the major impetus for the theory of multiple authorship
of Isaiah. I believe that Isaiah is written by only one author and that God not only reveals the future
of the Assyrian Empire, but also that of the Neo-Babylonian and the Persian Empires through this 8th
century B.C. prophet.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHECY (OT)

- This particular reference to Cyrus has to do with his decree of 538 B.C. that
allowed all of the exiled people (exiled by Assyria and Neo-Babylon) to return to their native
lands and rebuild their national temples with the help of the Persian treasury. For the specific
reference to the Jewish return see Ezra 1:2-4; 6:3-5. Cyrus' primary motivation for this was for
each of the nations to pray to their own god on Persia's behalf and Cyrus' successors (cf. Ezra 6:10; 7:23).

- I think that Isaiah 45:6 is extremely significant. It shows again not only the purpose of God
choosing Israel, but also of God choosing Cyrus. God chose Abraham to choose the world
and He chose Cyrus for the same larger purpose.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

- Notice the number of times the different words for create are used.

- BDB 427, KB 428 ‒ form, create, Isa. 44:24; 45:7,9 (twice), 18 (twice)

- BDB 793, KB 889 ‒ do, make, Isa. 44:24; 45:7,9,11,18

- BDB 135, KB 153 ‒ create, Isa. 45:7 (twice), 8,12,18 (twice)

The theological emphases of this "new age" section are

- YHWH alone created everything

- YHWH formed Israel for a purpose

- YHWH is alone and unique (monotheism)

- YHWH proves His existence by

- predictive prophecy

- Israel's existence

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 44:24-28

24Thus says the Lord, your Redeemer, and the one who formed you from the womb,

"I, the Lord, am the maker of all things,

Stretching out the heavens by Myself

And spreading out the earth all alone,

25Causing the omens of boasters to fail,

Making fools out of diviners,

Causing wise men to draw back

And turning their knowledge into foolishness,

26Confirming the word of His servant

And performing the purpose of His messengers.

It is I who says of Jerusalem, 'She shall be inhabited!'

And of the cities of Judah, 'They shall be built.'

And I will raise up her ruins again.

27It is I who says to the depth of the sea, 'Be dried up!'

And I will make your rivers dry.

28It is I who says of Cyrus, 'He is My shepherd!

And he will perform all My desire.'

And he declares of Jerusalem, 'She will be built,'

And of the temple, 'Your foundation will be laid.'"

44:24-28 This is one sentence in Hebrew. It is a series of relative clauses which are translated
by the NIV as "who. . ." It is significant that this is a structured unit (i.e. Isa. 44:24-45:13) because the
climax is found in the mention of Cyrus II by name in Isa. 45:28. It is basically a unit dealing with "the God
who can" versus the idols who cannot. YHWH announces beforehand what will occur to prove His
existence and power (cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 44:7,26).

Notice the list of "who. . ." in NIV (i.e. Qal PARTICIPLES).

- who formed you in the womb, Isa. 45:24

- who has made all things, Isa. 45:24

- who alone stretched out the heavens, Isa. 45:24

- who spread out the earth by Myself, Isa. 45:24

- who foils the signs of false prophets, Isa. 45:25

- who overthrows the learning of the wise, Isa. 45:25

- who carries out the words of his servants, Isa. 45:26

- who says of Jerusalem, "it shall be inhabited," Isa. 45:26

- who says to the watery deep, "Be dry," Isa. 45:27

- who says of Cyrus, "He is my shepherd," Isa. 45:28

44:24 Redeemer" This is the term Go'el, which has the same definition as "ransom"
with the added idea of a near kinsman as the agent. It is often a title for God (cf. Job 19:25; Ps. 19:15; 78:35;
Isa. 41:14; 43:14; 44:6,24; 49:7; 59:20; Jer. 50:34); it is used in this personal sense to reveal God's character
and Israel as His chosen special family.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "the one who formed you from the womb" This is imagery referring to the formation
of the nation of Israel (cf. Isa. 45:2). It is used uniquely of the Exodus experience. This concept of
birthing also lends itself to the concept of the people of God as the children of God.

▣ "I, the Lord, am. . ." This is literally the phrase, "I am YHWH,"
which is a key phrase in the OT. It is a play on the covenant name for God, from the VERB
"to be" (cf. Exod. 3:14). Its basic meaning is "I am the ever-existing, only-existing God."

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

▣ "maker of all things" This is the emphasis of God as both Creator (cf. Psalm 104) and Redeemer (cf. Isa. 45:12,18; Psalm 103).

▣ "Stretching out the heavens by Myself" Here again is God as Creator. This phraseology
is used in Isa. 40:22; 42:5; 45:12,18; 51:13.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE CIRCLE OF THE EARTH

▣

NASB
"all alone"

NKJV, Peshitta (Qere)
"by Myself"

NRSV, DSS, LXX, TEV
"no one helped me"

NJB
"who was with me?"

REB
"alone"

JPSOA
"unaided"

NET
"all by myself"

The MT has "who with me" (Ketiv), which parallels "alone" (BDB 94 II) in the
previous line of poetry. The Masoretic Text scholars suggested "by myself" (Qere). No one gave YHWH
counsel or suggestions when He created the earth (cf. Job 38:4ff).

Some scholars see the "Us" of Gen. 1:26; 3:22; 11:7, as referring to an angelic council, but even if
this is true, this text asserts YHWH Himself created and performed these things (cf. "by myself" and "all alone").

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAVENLY COUNCIL OF ANGELIC BEINGS

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

44:25 "omens. . .diviners. . .wise men" This verse is an exposure of the occult practices of
the surrounding nations, particularly Neo-Babylon. It is a literary foil for God to discuss His true prophets in
Isa. 45:26. Biblically, the way to determine a true prophet is found in Deut. 13:1-3; 18:22. The false
prophets and the true prophets are going to be contrasted in order to reveal that God is the only God.

It is possible that the Hebrew word translated "boasters" in the NASB can mean (i.e. "the omens of boasters")

- liars, vain talkers (BDB 95 III)

- soothsayers, from an Akkadian root (AB, vol. 20, p. 72), which would make it parallel
to "diviners" (line 2). The Barim priests of Neo-Babylon were known for their predictions (Leupold, p. 133).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

44:26 "Confirming the word of His servant" God is in control of history. His forth-telling
of future events is one way to prove to all mankind that YHWH is the only Creator, Redeemer God
(cf. Isa. 41:22-23; 45:7,26; see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE
[its uniqueness and inspiration]). Throughout this section of Isaiah prophecy is used as a means of God
demonstrating His ability over against the inability of the occult practices to determine future events.

The words "servant" (BDB 712) and "messengers" (BDB 521) are parallel. The first is
SINGULAR (UBS Text Project, p. 122, gives the SINGULAR a "B" rating)
and the second PLURAL. Is this meant to refer to

- the Servant

- the prophets (NET Bible)

or are both to be understood as the prophet? Thereby, "servant" would be a
way to characterize all prophets.

This verse may be an allusion to Isa. 2:2-4 or Micah 4:1-4.

▣ "It is I who says of Jerusalem, 'she shall be inhabited'" This is a very
specific prophecy of not only the restoration of Jerusalem but also of the cities of Judah
(cf. Isa. 2:2-4; Dan. 2:24-27; Mic. 4:1-3).

44:27 There has been much discussion on the meaning of this verse. These are the theories:

- YHWH controls the waters of chaos (cf. Genesis 1; Psalm 74:12-17; Isa. 51:10).

- It is a reference to God's splitting of the Red Sea and the Jordan River and, therefore,
is a reference to the Exodus.

- It shows that God can overcome any barrier and is used in the sense of God drying up
or overcoming the Euphrates River (i.e. note Isa. 11:15-16) so that Cyrus can defeat Babylon.

- This is used in some sense that God is the controller of moisture which proves that He, and not Ba'al,
is the true fertility God, the God of abundance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA

44:28 "It is I who says of Cyrus" Cyrus is mentioned by name for the first time in this context. He
is also mentioned by name in Isa. 45:1. Josephus, in his book, Antiquities of the Jews, 11.1.2, says
that Jewish tradition believes that these prophecies were shown to Cyrus and because of them he allowed
the Jews to return to Judah. We also learn that Cyrus was impressed by these prophecies in 2 Chr. 36:22-23.

▣ "He is My shepherd" This term primarily speaks of a leader or administrator. There are
two very strong kingly terms used here, "shepherd" (BDB 944 I) in Isa. 44:28 and "anointed one" (BDB 603)
in Isa. 45:1. Both of these terms show that God will use Cyrus to accomplish His larger purposes. This does not
imply that Cyrus became a believer (cf. Isa. 45:5c), but that God uses human instrumentality in order to
accomplish His purposes (i.e. Exod. 3:7-10).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE, F. #4

▣ "Your foundation will be laid" The fulfillment of this prophecy, related to both the city of
Jerusalem and the temple, is found in the books of Ezra, Nehemiah, Daniel (i.e. Dan. 9:24-27), and Haggai.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 45:1-7

1Thus says the Lord to Cyrus His anointed,

Whom I have taken by the right hand,

To subdue nations before him

And to loose the loins of kings;

To open doors before him so that gates will not be shut:

2"I will go before you and make the rough places smooth;

I will shatter the doors of bronze and cut through their iron bars.

3I will give you the treasures of darkness

And hidden wealth of secret places,

So that you may know that it is I,

The Lord, the God of Israel, who calls you by your name.

4For the sake of Jacob My servant,

And Israel My chosen one,

I have also called you by your name;

I have given you a title of honor

Though you have not known Me.

5I am the Lord, and there is no other;

Besides Me there is no God.

I will gird you, though you have not known Me;

6That men may know from the rising to the setting of the sun

That there is no one besides Me.

I am the Lord, and there is no other,

7The One forming light and creating darkness,

Causing well-being and creating calamity;

I am the Lord who does all these."
